## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix mixed-case writes so entries remain readable through the cache’s case-insensitive lookup.

## Changes
The pull request adds `Cache.set()` and raises the default TTL from 60 to 300 seconds. It adds tests for round-trip lookup, expiration, and the default TTL constant.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Normalize keys before storing entries — After `set("Alpha", 1)`, `get("Alpha")` returns `None`. The write stores `"Alpha"` as supplied, while lookup lowercases the key. — Callers that write mixed-case keys cannot retrieve those entries through the public API.

## Suggestions
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Expire entries at their deadline — With `Cache(ttl=0)`, `get("alpha")` returns a just-written value if both calls see the same clock reading. The write sets the deadline to that reading, and the strict `<` check accepts equality. — Callers using a zero TTL can receive a cached value after its configured lifetime has elapsed. — Fix: Treat equality as expired at `app/cache.py:21`.
- app/cache.py:7 — comments — Describe 300 seconds as the default TTL — For `Cache(ttl=1)`, the comment says “Entries expire 300 seconds after they are written,” but the write uses `time.monotonic() + self._ttl`, which sets a one-second lifetime. — Callers reading the comment can expect entries with a custom TTL to remain available for five minutes.
- tests/test_cache.py:18 — tests — Test the default TTL through cache expiry — If `Cache()` reverts to a 60-second lifetime while `DEFAULT_TTL` stays at `300`, the test still passes because its sole assertion reads the class constant. — The cache tests would miss a regression that evicts entries four minutes earlier than intended.
